evidence: SOURCE: (1) Real gates in the gate dimensions. task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:17-24 hro_gate_render (binary): an incorrect password leaves the visitor signed out, then the correct password for a seeded Recruiter shows a usable staff workspace with navigation and readable content; 'A static picture or only a health response is insufficient.' This is the auth leg. task/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:17-24 hro_gate_shared (binary): a Recruiter opens a new job and adds a candidate through ordinary UI, then in a new independent empty browser context the Observer finds the same job and exactly one card for that candidate in Applied; 'A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate.' This is the server-backing leg with independent-context readback, as REVIEW_POLICY 'Gates must exclude convincing dead apps' requires. Both gates use aggregation all_pass, scoring.toml:1-3 sets gates render/constraints = 0.0, and score.py:40-48 sets reward 0.0 unless every gate score exceeds its floor. (2) Every scored prompt carries the in-dimension gate. functional/prompt.md:9-13 '## Global browser gate and independent scoring' repeats the sign-in, UI create and independent-context Observer readback; line 13: 'A blank or static shell, an unavailable app or an observed failure of that check gives every binary criterion 0.' polish/prompt.md:9-12 runs the same check: 'A blank or static shell or an observed failure of that check gives binary0 throughout.' visual/prompt.md:9-12 runs the same check: '... gives every criterion its minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero.' All three hard-zero on gate failure, and none gives partial credit, which is the quality-checks.md defect. The scored gates include an auth leg (Recruiter/Observer sign-in through ordinary controls) and a backing leg (independent-context readback). (3) No same-origin requirement. A grep for 'origin|cors' across task/tests, instruction.md and environment/instructions finds only the word 'original' (functional judge.toml:209). instruction.md:13 explicitly allows the browser side to pull fonts or scripts from a CDN. The internal-sheet wording 'cross-origin apps' is the older version; the public row, the SKILL delivery profile and staged-task-contract all forbid a same-origin requirement, and the task follows them. (4) Public basis. Sign-in, roles (Recruiter, Observer), a job with title, team, hiring manager and places, and a candidate with name, email and source come from instruction.md:17 and hireops_rules.md sections 1-2 (lines 11-33). app_context.md:10-16 lists the accounts. The Observer 'reads everything', so the Observer readback of a new job is a fair public behaviour, and the gate accepts 'another working staff account' as a fallback. COUNTEREXAMPLE ATTEMPTS: (a) Each plausible broken app fails at least one gate: a localStorage-only store (no independent-context readback), a success toast without persistence, a static board of seed data (the new job and card are absent elsewhere), an app with no or permissive auth (the render wrong-password leg), and a health-only server. (b) For conforming alternatives, routes and labels are free ('Discover routes and controls by intent'), with 'any hiring manager', 'any source' and a staff-account fallback for the Observer. I found no conforming design that the gate wrongly zeros. Minor wording point, not a defect: the scored-prompt gate text names title, hiring manager and places but not team or source, which the rules make part of a job and a candidate. A judge would fill required fields, and the constraints gate names them. Template comparison: the template render gate also checks 'no protected data is visible before sign-in', and the task gate omits that check. Anonymous refusal is graded in functional hro_anonymous instead, which is acceptable task tailoring rather than a missing gate. The task gate prompts also drop the template's line allowing external font, script and CDN requests, but nothing in them contradicts it. RUNTIME: the raw-evidence-index scope says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The scripted golden driver (workspace.cjs:285-330 and 495-510; 25/25 results passed; no page errors) shows the wrong-password refusal, opening a job and adding a candidate through the UI, and an Observer in a separate browser.newContext reading the board. It does not run the exact gate recipe, a configured claude-code judge, or a dead or static app through the gates. The browser_run_code_unsafe independent-context recipe has only been shown working under @playwright/mcp 0.0.79 in another task's evidence (deliverables/colderwater-playground-devtools/coverage-fix-2026-09-27/golden/MCP_RECIPE_COMPATIBILITY.json), not for this task. RISK=true because the gate's actual effect is unmeasured. Nothing shows the golden passing all five gates under the configured judge or a static or browser-only app being zeroed. If the independent-context step failed for tooling reasons, each prompt maps it to binary0 or Likert 1 'NOT EXERCISED', which would zero a conforming app.
